card.name: Dose formulas and quantity phrases
card.fires_on: Words that sit just before a number or amount in dosing text, such as 'formula' after 'per 120 mL of', an opening bracket in a dose equation, or 'increased' and 'maximum' before a figure.

modes.label: Dose equations
modes.description: An opening bracket or equals sign that starts a calculation or a scale.
modes.example: Adult and pediatric patients 12 years or older: CLcr (mL/min) =<< [>>140 - age (years)]

modes.label: Per-volume dosing
modes.description: The noun that ends a 'per X mL of' phrase for a dose.
modes.example: The recommended oral dosage is 4,000 lipase units per 120 mL of<< formula>> or per breastfeeding.

modes.label: Change or limit words
modes.description: Verbs or nouns like increased or maximum that come before a quantity.
modes.example: the dose was<< increased>> daily to a mean dose of 4
